text:
maria: Quick question — we're seeing odd 502s when a customer uses our Node SDK inside a private VPC with an outbound proxy. They set CLIENT_BASE_URL to https://private-inference.company.local and also route via their corporate proxy. Any precedence rules we should call out?

kai: hmm usually base URL should win for request host, but proxy env var (HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY) can force traffic through. Are they using NO_PROXY for the private host?

maria: not initially. they just set HTTPS_PROXY to http://proxy.corp:3128 and left NO_PROXY blank.

ben: that explains a lot. proxy rewrites the Host header sometimes, and some internal SNI configs expect the original host. If the proxy doesn't pass SNI or Host through, backend rejects -> 502.

lisa: recommended customer config: set BASE_URL to private endpoint, and add that hostname to NO_PROXY so traffic goes direct inside the VPC. if they must go through proxy, ensure it supports TLS passthrough and preserves SNI.

ash: small note on SDK behavior: our clients prefer explicit baseURL passed to constructor over env var, but env var still used as fallback. i.e. new Redwood({ baseURL }) > process.env.RW_BASE_URL. also HTTP_PROXY is honored by underlying http client libs.

maria: could you paste the Node example of how they'd set NO_PROXY so I can forward?

kai: quick snippet: 

export HTTPS_PROXY="http://proxy.corp:3128"
export NO_PROXY="private-inference.company.local,10.0.0.0/8"
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, baseURL: process.env.CLIENT_BASE_URL })

ben: for Python it's similar. requests respects NO_PROXY from env, and urllib3 pooled connections won't attempt proxy if host matches NO_PROXY pattern.

maria: we also saw streaming sessions drop mid-response; think it's related to proxy keepalive timeouts. Any quick mitigations?

ash: streaming over HTTP/1.1 long lived connections are fragile behind corporate proxies. two options: (1) move streaming to direct path (NO_PROXY), (2) enable reconnect logic on the client side with resume semantics.

lisa: for Node SDK we added a reconnect backoff for SSE/websocket streams — it tries 2 retries with a fresh HTTP agent to avoid reusing a half-closed socket. If you need we can open a small patch to make that configurable per-instance.

maria: customer can't direct route. they want transparent proxy. what debug data should i ask for?

ben: ask for: curl -v --resolve private-inference.company.local:443:10.1.2.3 https://private-inference.company.local/health (shows TLS/SNI and direct reachability), proxy logs for CONNECT handling, and a capture of client debug logs (set RW_DEBUG=trace) showing headers and socket errors.

kai: also ask them to curl via proxy: 

curl -v -x http://proxy.corp:3128 https://private-inference.company.local/health

that shows whether proxy CONNECT preserves TLS.

maria: perfect. any server-side header toggles we can accept?

ash: we can accept Host override in header, but SNI must match cert SAN. so if proxy terminates TLS we need PKI that proxy trusts and reissues certs (mTLS in corp env). Better to avoid terminator.

lisa: and FYI for future docs: add a short checklist "VPC + proxy common gotchas" — NO_PROXY, SNI passthrough, mTLS, socket keepalive timeouts, SDK reconnect config. I'll add to the devex cookbook.

deploy-bot: reminder — there's a patch in progress to expose streamReconnectAttempts as client config (PR #4123).

maria: thanks all. i'll gather customer logs and try NO_PROXY first, then coordinate if they need SDK toggle. :thumbsup:
